lines.text: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine hits, and Elimelech takes his wife Naomi and his sons Mahlon and Chilion to live in the land of Moab.
Elimelech dies, the sons marry Orpah and Rachel, and after about ten years both sons die too, so Naomi is left without her husband and her two sons.
Naomi hears that the LORD has provided food for His people, so she heads back toward Judah, and on the road she tells Orpah and Ruth to go home, and Ruth kisses her goodbye while Orpah clings to her.

wrong_details.wrong: Ruth kisses her goodbye while Orpah clings to her
wrong_details.true: Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her

lines.text: Ruth tells Naomi, "your people will be my people, and your God will be my God," and when Naomi sees that Ruth is determined, she stops trying to persuade her.
Naomi and Ruth reach Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest, and Naomi tells the women to call her Mara because she went away full and the LORD has brought her back empty.
